checkuser-clienthints-name-architecture: This is shown as a prefix to the 'architecture' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'architecture' Client Hints data value is what the CPU architecture of the device is (for example arm, x86).
checkuser-clienthints-name-bitness: This is shown as a prefix to the 'bitness' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The "bitness" Client Hints data value is the "bitness" (size of an integer in memory) of the device CPU (for example 64 or 32). This is also often named "word size" in English and some other languages; see [[w:en:Word (computer architecture)|Word (computer architecture)]] on the English Wikipedia.
checkuser-clienthints-name-form-factor: This is shown as a prefix to the 'form factor' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'form factor' Client Hints data value gives information about the form-factor of the device (such as 'Mobile', 'Tablet', 'Desktop').
checkuser-clienthints-name-brand: This is shown as a prefix to the 'brand' and 'fullVersionList' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'brand' and 'fullVersionList' Client Hints data values give information about the different brands associated with a browser, including a version number. Examples of the values for this data are 'Google Chrome 115' and 'Opera 114'. This is also used as the prefix for the 'userAgent' Client Hints value.
checkuser-clienthints-name-mobile:
This is shown as a prefix to the 'mobile' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'mobile' Client Hints data value can either be 'yes' or 'no' to indicate whether the device being used was a mobile device.

See also:
*{{msg-mw|checkuser-clienthints-value-yes}} and {{msg-mw|checkuser-clienthints-value-no}} are the values that can be shown after this prefix.
checkuser-clienthints-name-model: This is shown as a prefix to the 'model' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'model' Client Hints data value gives the model number of the device and is usually just set for mobile devices (for example, 'Redmi Note 8' or 'SM-A115F').
checkuser-clienthints-name-platform: This is shown as a prefix to the combined 'platform' and 'platformVersion' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'platform' Client Hints data value gives gives the OS brand name (such as 'Windows') and the 'platformVersion' gives the OS version number (such as 15.0.0).
checkuser-clienthints-name-platform-vers: This is shown as a prefix for the 'platformVersion' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string and when the 'platform' Client Hints data value was not provided. The 'platformVersion' Client Hints data value gives the operating system version number (such as 15.0.0).
checkuser-clienthints-name-wow64:
{{notranslate}}
This is shown as a prefix to the 'WoW64' Client Hints data in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The 'WoW64' Client Hints data value can either be 'yes' or 'no' and indicates whether the device is running in 32-bit mode on 64-bit Windows.
checkuser-clienthints-name-is-browser:
{{notranslate}}
This is shown as a prefix for the value of the x-is-browser header in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The x-is-browser header stores how likely a action was performed by a browser.
checkuser-clienthints-name-ja3n:
{{notranslate}}
This is shown as a prefix for the value of the x-ja3n header in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The x-ja3n Client Hints data value is a string that gives information about the TLS fingerprint of the client.
checkuser-clienthints-name-ja4h:
{{notranslate}}
This is shown as a prefix for the value of the x-ja4h header in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The x-ja4h Client Hints data value is a string that gives information about the TLS fingerprint of the client.
checkuser-clienthints-name-api-user-agen:
{{notranslate}}
This is shown as a prefix for the value of the Api-User-Agent header in Special:CheckUser and Special:Investigate when displaying the Client Hints data as a concatenated string. The Api-User-Agent header is how a script that runs in a browser identifies itself in an API request.
checkuser-clienthints-value-yes: This is used as the value for 'mobile' and 'WoW64' when the value sent indicated that it the device was mobile or the device was running in 32-bit mode on 64-bit Windows respectively.
checkuser-clienthints-value-no: This is used as the value for 'mobile' and 'WoW64' when the value sent indicated that it the device was not a mobile device or the device is not running in 32-bit mode on 64-bit Windows respectively.
checkuser-clienthints-value-is-browser-l: This is used as the value for 'isBrowser' when the value is 20 or below.
checkuser-clienthints-value-is-browser-i: This is used as the value for 'isBrowser' when the value is 21 to 79.
checkuser-clienthints-value-is-browser-l: This is used as the value for 'isBrowser' when the value is 80 or above.
checkuser-clienthints-list-item:
{{optional}}
This is used to combine the messages that start with 'checkuser-clienthints-name-' (such as {{msg-mw|checkuser-clienthints-name-mobile}}) with the associated value.
Parameters:
* $1 - The Client Hint 'name' (e.g. {{msg-mw|checkuser-clienthints-name-mobile}})
* $2 - The Client Hint 'value' (e.g. {{msg-mw|checkuser-clienthints-value-yes}}).

* $4 - a formatted date of the event
